title: Isolated hydatid cyst in a single moiety of an incomplete duplex kidney
case_text:
A 13-year old female presented with continuous dull pain localized to the right flank region for three months. She had no urinary complaints. General examination was unremarkable. Abdominal examination revealed a 10 cms x 10 cms lump in the right lumbar region which was bimanually palpable. Her routine blood and urine investigations were normal with no eosinophilia, and had normal renal function tests. X-ray chest was normal. Ultrasonography whole abdomen suggested a heterogeneous cyst of size 13 cms x 10 cms with multiple daughter cysts and septation in the right lobe of liver with non-visualisation of right kidney. Contrast Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) showed a large multiloculated cyst of size 11.5cms x 10.5cms x 15.5cms with internal septations arising from the upper pole of right kidney, with typical cysts within cyst appearance and thinned out peripheral parenchyma. Liver was pushed upwards and medially, which otherwise was normal (Fig.1). ELISA test for echinococcus antibodies was positive. A course of albendazole was given for one month and subsequently patient was planned for surgery.
On exploration, there was a large hydatid cyst in the upper moiety of right incomplete duplex kidney, compressing the lower moiety into thin rim of parenchyma with two separate ureters that were united caudally. Heminephrectomy was not feasible, so a simple nephrectomy was done. Cut specimen of the right kidney had two moieties with two ureters. The upper moiety was turned into a bag of cysts while lower moiety had compressed thinned out renal parenchyma with no evidence of any cystic disease (Fig. 2,3). The histopathological examination of the cyst was consistent with the diagnosis of hydatid disease of kidney. Albendazole was continued for eight weeks after surgery. USG abdomen after 6 months suggested no recurrence.

You are an expert clinician–educator in tropical and infectious diseases.
Your job is to transform a published clinical case report into a standardized admission diagnostic teaching case following the Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology.

In terms of style, model your output on NEJM’s Clinicopathologic Conferences ("Case Records of the Massachusetts General Hospital").

RULES (Read Carefully — No Exceptions):
1. SOURCE FIDELITY:
   - Extract facts ONLY from the supplied case report.
   - Do NOT invent, embellish, or smooth out missing clinical data.
   - Never extrapolate findings not explicitly mentioned.

2. THE ADMISSION BREAKPOINT PRINCIPLE (CRITICAL):
   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Echinococcosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: hydatid cyst in an incomplete duplex kidney
